title: Bioreactors & Tissue Culture Engineering
description: Scale cell culture and tissue maturation through mass transfer, shear, process monitoring, control, sterility-boundary reasoning, and design-of-experiments principles.

modifications: Broadened outcome 2 to state scale-up constraints explicitly and linked the four original lesson pairs to outcomes 2–4. Corrected the oxygen-demand and mixing-scale question associations; added direct impeller Reynolds-number practice. Existing questions and numeric keys are unchanged. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added bounded sterile-boundary and contamination-evidence reasoning to existing week 12, with one synthetic log-reduction calculation, two distinct formative checks and three retrieval cards. No process settings, sterilization procedures or real-process claims are provided; the schedule remains 14 weeks and the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

outcomes.description: Estimate oxygen-transfer, mixing, shear, and scale-up constraints.
Interpret growth kinetics and process data.
Design controls and acceptance criteria for a reproducible process.

lesson_objectives.description: Fit a simple exponential growth model over its valid phase.
Calculate doubling time and identify when exponential assumptions fail.
Apply an oxygen transfer balance.
Compare oxygen transfer capacity to cellular demand.
Estimate Reynolds number and mixing-time tradeoffs.
Use dimensionless similarity only when the relevant constraints are preserved.
Choose critical process parameters and quality attributes.
Separate process drift from assay variation.
Map contamination entry routes and interpret sterility evidence within its limits.
Compute the maximum oxygen transfer rate and the cell density it can support from kLa, saturation concentration, a critical dissolved-oxygen level and specific uptake.
Compare strategies for raising oxygen supply with their side effects.
Evaluate an empirical kLa correlation's domain of validity.
Write mass balances for cells, a consumed substrate and a secreted product in a batch culture using specific rates.
Integrate the substrate balance for an exponentially growing population to predict substrate remaining, product formed and the time of exhaustion.
Extend the balance to a perfused vessel with dilution, and evaluate the assumptions behind constant specific rates and yields.
Compute the specific growth rate from Monod kinetics and the nutrient level that gives a target fraction of the maximum rate.
Compute the yield-limited maximum cell density and the minimum time to reach it.
Evaluate what the single-nutrient Monod model and a constant yield leave out for animal cell culture.
Compute the steady-state nutrient and cell concentrations of a chemostat and the washout dilution rate.
Find the dilution rate that maximizes cell output and compare operating points.
Compute cell-specific perfusion rates and evaluate what they require of a perfused culture.
Compute the power input, power per volume, Reynolds number and tip speed of a stirred vessel.
Apply the scaling laws for geometrically similar vessels under constant power per volume, constant tip speed and constant speed.
Evaluate the trade-offs between criteria and explain why scale-down models are used.
Convert power per volume into an energy dissipation rate, a Kolmogorov scale and a stress at that scale.
Compare the eddy scale with the size of a cell or microcarrier and compute a stirring level that keeps eddies above a chosen size.
Evaluate why average power per volume, tip speed and local dissipation give different pictures of shear.
Compute the oxygen uptake rate and the kLa required to hold a dissolved-oxygen setpoint as a culture grows.
Find the time at which a vessel reaches its capacity and compare the options for extending it.
Evaluate a dissolved-oxygen control cascade, the oxygen time constant and the role of sensor lag.
Compute main effects and interactions from a two-level factorial design.
Estimate the standard error of an effect and the curvature from center-point replicates.
Evaluate a design for aliasing, randomization and the unit of replication.
Summarize replicate gassing-out runs by agitation speed.
Estimate kLa from the dissolved-oxygen curve and its dependence on agitation speed.
Evaluate the cell density a measured kLa can support and the limits of the method, including probe response.
Estimate the oxygen excursion a cell experiences in a poorly mixed zone and compare it with the critical level and with the mixing time.
Design a scale-down experiment as a two-by-two comparison of environment and passage, and compute its effects and interaction.
Plan the replication and sampling, including the independent unit, the number of cultures and the measurements.
Solve a declared synthetic biomass/product reaction using separate elemental balances.
Calculate biomass and product yields and verify carbon recovery from a balanced reaction.
Distinguish stoichiometric yields from Monod kinetics and state limitations of the synthetic reaction.
Write fed-batch balances with a changing volume and explain why a dilution term D = F/V appears in the concentration equations without any outflow.
Calculate an exponential feed that holds a substrate at a set point, the cumulative feed volume and the time at which the vessel reaches its working volume.
Compare batch, fed-batch and continuous operation for cell concentration, product titer and dilution, and state what a single-substrate feed model omits.

duration.equivalent_structure: Proposed 14-week undergraduate scope only. Three compact prototype units remain in weeks 5, 9 and 12 beside the expanded week-1 growth and balance primer and original lessons on growth kinetics, the culture mass balance, continuous and perfused culture, oxygen supply and its control, scale-up, shear, and design of experiments; week 7 is a synthetic-data lab on measuring kLa and week 14 a lesson on designing a scale-down experiment, which prepares the course case. Weeks 8–9 add an optional oxygen-capacity project with rehearsal practice and milestone self-checks. All activities are open, ungraded practice. There are no graded homework sets, exams or graded project, and workload has not been measured, so this schedule is not evidence of semester equivalence.

modules.title: Growth kinetics and process mass balance

lessons.title: Growth kinetics and process mass balance
lessons.worked_example: If viable concentration rises from 0.5 to 2.0 million cells/mL over 48 h, the fourfold increase gives μ=ln(4)/48=0.0289 h⁻¹ and a doubling time of 24 h. In a synthetic fixed-volume balance, 2.0×10⁹ viable cells with μ=0.030 h⁻¹ and loss rate 0.005 h⁻¹ accumulate at 5.0×10⁷ cells/h when flows are absent. These are interval-specific estimates under stated assumptions, not universal cell-line rates.

lessons.title: Oxygen transfer and consumption
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic culture at 2×10⁶ viable cells/mL with qO₂=1×10⁻¹⁶ mol/(cell·s) has an uptake rate of 0.72 mmol/(L·h). Separately, kLa=10 h⁻¹ and a 0.10 mmol/L driving force give OTR=1.00 mmol/(L·h); if OUR is 1.50, the bulk oxygen balance is −0.50 mmol/(L·h).

lessons.title: Mixing, shear, and scale-up
lessons.worked_example: For a geometrically similar 2 L to 200 L scale-up, the characteristic length factor is 100^(1/3)=4.64. Constant tip speed gives a rotational-speed ratio of 0.215, while idealized turbulent constant power per volume gives 0.359 and raises tip speed by about 1.67; the criteria cannot preserve every transport condition together.

lessons.title: Process monitoring, control, and quality
lessons.worked_example: A dissolved-oxygen probe that drifts low can trigger a control response that changes agitation even if the culture state has not changed. An independent calibrated measurement or reference check can help distinguish sensor bias from a true oxygen change, provided location and response time are considered. Separately, a reference assay staying within ±2% while batch titre falls 20% makes the represented assay variation an unlikely sole explanation, but does not establish the process cause. In a separate synthetic example, a stipulated 1.2×10⁶ starting count with a modeled four-log reduction leaves 120 modeled survivors, not a validated process result.

lessons.title: Sizing oxygen supply in a culture: kLa, driving force and the cell density a reactor can support
lessons.worked_example: OTR_max = 5.0 × (0.2 − 0.05) = 0.75 mmol/(L·h), which supports 3.75×10⁶ cells/mL at 2.0×10⁻¹⁰ mmol per cell per hour; doubling kLa doubles it, and 50% oxygen gas gives 2.25 mmol/(L·h).

lessons.title: Writing a cell-culture mass balance: substrate use, product accumulation and when a batch runs out
lessons.worked_example: From 5.0×10⁵ cells/mL at μ = 0.03 h⁻¹, 48 h of growth consumes 10.74 mM glucose and makes 17.2 mM lactate; 25 mM glucose is exhausted at about 71 h; perfusion of 5.0×10⁶ cells/mL needs D ≥ 0.040 h⁻¹.

modules.title: Monod growth, yield and elemental stoichiometry

lessons.title: Growth kinetics: Monod saturation, yield and what limits a batch
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic culture with μ_max 0.05 per hour and K_s 1.0 mM grows at 0.0333 per hour at 2 mM, needs 4.0 mM glucose for 80% of its maximum rate, and can reach at most 1.25 × 10⁶ cells/mL from 3.0 × 10⁵ cells/mL, taking at least 28.5 h; the lesson's culture reaches 3.05 × 10⁶ cells/mL in at least 68.1 h.

lessons.title: Element-balanced biomass and product yields
lessons.worked_example: For one mole of glucose, the stipulated balance forms 2 C-mol biomass, 1 mol symbolic product, 2 mol CO2 and consumes 0.9 mol O2; C, H, O and N totals close exactly under the stated empirical formulas and fixed synthetic reaction coefficients.

lessons.title: Continuous and perfused culture: chemostat steady states, washout and cell-specific perfusion
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic chemostat with μ_max 0.05 per hour, K_s 1.0 mM and 10 mM feed washes out above 0.0455 per hour; at D = 0.03 per hour the steady state is 1.50 mM glucose and 0.850 × 10⁶ cells/mL (a residence time of 33.3 h); the lesson's chemostat has D_crit 0.0390 and maximum output near 0.0338 per hour, and its perfusion culture needs at least 240 pL/(cell·day).

lessons.title: Mixing and scale-up: power, tip speed and what cannot be kept constant
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic 1 L vessel with a 5 cm impeller at 240 rpm draws 30.0 W/m³; scaled by 5 in linear dimension at constant power per volume it runs at 82.1 rpm, its tip speed rises 1.71-fold and its mixing time 2.92-fold; the 2 L lab vessel scaled by 10 at constant P/V reaches 1.35 m/s and 27.8 s.

lessons.title: Shear, eddies and cells: the Kolmogorov scale and when stirring becomes damage
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic vessel at 50 W/m³ has ε = 0.050 W/kg and an average Kolmogorov scale of 51.2 μm; with a local factor of 50 the scale near the impeller is 19.2 μm and the stress 1.32 Pa, well below a 100 μm carrier; the lab vessel at 21.6 W/m³ would need an average of about 0.5 W/m³ to keep local eddies at 50 μm.

lessons.title: Controlling dissolved oxygen: the required kLa, the capacity limit and the control cascade
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic culture needs kLa 0.75 per hour at the start and, growing at 0.025 per hour, reaches a 4 per hour ceiling after 67.0 h at 2.13 × 10⁶ cells/mL with a 15 min oxygen time constant; the lesson's culture reaches its ceiling after 53.6 h at 2.5 × 10⁶ cells/mL, or after 99.9 h and 10 × 10⁶ cells/mL with oxygen enrichment.

lessons.title: Design of experiments: factorial designs, effects, interactions and replication
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic 2² design with runs 2.0, 3.0, 2.6 and 4.2 g/L has effects A = 1.30, B = 0.90 and interaction AB = 0.30, and a five-factor full design needs 32 runs against 16 for its half fraction; in the 2³ experiment of the lesson, temperature has the main effect 1.075, the AC interaction is 0.275, the effect standard error is 0.0707 and the curvature 0.2375.

lessons.title: Fed-batch culture: changing volume, dilution and feeding to hold a substrate
lessons.worked_example: Starting from 5.0 × 10⁸ cells in 1.0 L with μ = 0.03 h⁻¹ and q_G = 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ mmol per cell per hour, a 500 mM feed holding glucose at 5 mM needs 0.202 mL/h at t = 0 and 1.75 mL/h at 72 h, adds 51.7 mL by 72 h and fills a 1.5 L vessel at 144 h. At 72 h the concentration is 4.12 × 10⁶ cells/mL rather than 4.34 × 10⁶ because of dilution (D = 1.67 × 10⁻³ h⁻¹), and q_P = 1.0 × 10⁻¹² g per cell per hour gives a titer of 0.122 g/L. A constant feed equal to the initial demand supplies only half of the demand by 24 h.

lessons.title: Virtual lab 1: measuring kLa by dynamic gassing-out
lessons.worked_example: The synthetic gassing-out curves give kLa of 2.00, 3.67 and 5.66 per hour at 200, 300 and 400 rpm, an exponent of 1.50 in the speed (kLa roughly proportional to the square root of power per volume), a supportable density of 4.245 × 10⁶ cells/mL at 400 rpm and a probe-lag product of 0.031; a cell-free test is a starting estimate for a culture.

lessons.title: Separating a mixing limitation from cell-line instability: designing a scale-down experiment
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic culture at 6.0 × 10⁶ cells/mL with a 90 s mixing time loses 0.030 mmol/L of oxygen per visit to an unsupplied region and reaches the critical level after 150 s; a two-by-two scale-down with viabilities 92, 90, 80 and 78% has a loop effect of −2.0, a passage effect of −12.0 and an interaction of 0.0 points, favoring cell-line instability; the lesson's culture, with a 120 s mixing time, falls 0.067 mmol/L per visit, and a loop effect of −11.5 with 6 cultures per group needed for 80% power.

lessons.title: Oxygen project guide: transfer capacity against a growing demand (optional, ungraded)
lessons.worked_example: For a normalized model with k = 1.0, OUR₀ = 0.2, μ = 0.5 and Ccrit = 0.5, the deficit is D(t) = (0.2/1.5)(e^(0.5t) − e^(−t)). Demand equals threshold capacity 0.5 at t ≈ 1.833, but the dissolved oxygen is still about 0.688 then and first reaches the threshold at t ≈ 2.680.

assessments.title: Virtual lab 1: measuring kLa by dynamic gassing-out (ungraded practice)
Element-balanced biomass and product yield practice
Oxygen project rehearsal: deficit, capacity check and transient crossing (open, ungraded practice)
Oxygen project milestones M1–M5 in the Case studio (optional self-check; ungraded)

grading_policy.attempt_policy: Unlimited formative retries; no summative grade is awarded.
grading_policy.solution_release: Public practice solutions may be shown after an attempt. They are not production exam keys.
grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.
grading_policy.appeals: No instructor review workflow is implemented; report ambiguous practice items to repository maintainers.

accessibility.diagram_policy: The seed package contains no imported diagrams; newly authored diagrams require descriptions and individual license tracking.
known_issues: Unicode equations require structured mathematical alternatives and assistive-technology review.

history.summary: Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.

Added an original lesson on sizing oxygen supply (kLa, driving force, maximum supportable cell density, static-dish medium depth and the limits of empirical correlations) with six formative items with computed keys and four retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Added an original lesson on cell-culture mass balances (batch substrate use and product accumulation, time to exhaustion, perfusion balance) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Assessments with items now also list the course outcomes those items assess, derived from each item's lesson objective and that objective's outcome links. The rubric-only case lists none, and neither do the 4 prototype-unit assessments, whose objectives are not yet linked to an outcome. No readings, items or keys changed. The syllabus was regenerated from the manifest: it states the current version, lists every lesson with its item and card counts, and describes the current practice and limitations (it still described only the four original units). The course limitations shown to learners were also updated: they still described one formative check per lesson and the original numerical rules. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added a common-mistakes section to 1 original lesson that lacked one (bioreactors-5); each bullet names a mistake that the lesson's own text addresses. Fixed number formatting that an earlier authoring step left in learner-visible text: raw exponent notation (a number written with the letter e and a power of ten) and floating-point artifacts (a decimal with a long run of trailing digits) in a worked-example summary, item bioreactors-5:max-cell-density, item bioreactors-5:max-medium-depth, the oxygen-supply reading. No answer key, tolerance or objective changed. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added a proposed 14-week schedule; seven original lessons (Monod growth and yield; chemostat steady states, washout and cell-specific perfusion; mixing and scale-up; shear, eddies and the Kolmogorov scale; dissolved-oxygen control and the capacity limit; factorial design of experiments; and designing a scale-down experiment that separates a mixing limitation from cell-line instability, which prepares the course case); and a synthetic-data lab on measuring kLa by dynamic gassing-out. No new references were added. All activities remain ungraded practice; the package remains partial and unreviewed, gives no laboratory protocol or process recipe, and makes no claim about any cell line, vessel or process.

Expanded the week-1 growth reading with an interval-specific exponential model, viable-count versus total-cell balance, loss terms, substrate/product balances and unit-aware rate estimation. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. Three compact prototype readings remain in weeks 5, 9 and 12; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-5 oxygen reading with unit-aware transfer and uptake rates, a transient dissolved-oxygen balance, a target-concentration feasibility check and limits of bulk estimates. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. Two compact prototype readings remain in weeks 9 and 12; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-9 mixing reading with scale-up criteria, an idealized geometric-scaling comparison, links between gradients and cell exposure, and limits of scale-down inference. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. One compact prototype reading remains in week 12; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-12 process-monitoring reading with the parameter-to-quality chain, sensor/control distinctions, trend interpretation, predeclared acceptance criteria and traceable records. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. All four original compact prototype readings now have expanded primers; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Broadened outcome 2 to include scale-up constraints and linked the first four lesson pairs to outcomes 2–4. Corrected the oxygen-demand and scale-up question associations and added direct impeller Reynolds-number practice; existing questions and numeric keys are unchanged. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added an inactive, normalized oxygen-capacity project draft that derives a transient deficit under a growing demand and compares quasi-steady capacity with the actual threshold crossing. It does not repeat the existing kLa fit or specify a real process; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added a week-2 synthetic C/H/O/N balance for stipulated biomass and product formation alongside Monod kinetics. The worked equation yields 2 C-mol biomass and 1 mol symbolic product per mol glucose, with independent atom checks; nine formative items and four retrieval cards support the lesson. The schedule remains 14 weeks and the course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added sterile-boundary and contamination-evidence reasoning within the existing week-12 monitoring lesson. A synthetic log-reduction arithmetic example, two formative checks and three cards distinguish mapped entry routes from product attributes and state that neither a model nor a single negative sample proves batch sterility. No process instructions were added; the schedule remains 14 weeks and the course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added an original fed-batch reading grouped with continuous culture in week 4: amount and concentration balances with changing volume, the dilution term D = F/V without outflow, an exponential feed that holds a substrate at a set point, cumulative feed and the working-volume limit, titer with retained product, and a batch/fed-batch/chemostat comparison. Three objectives, ten formative items and four cards. MIT OCW 10.442 Spring 2005 lists bioreactor design after continuous culture; it is a link-only comparator. No week was added. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Made the planned oxygen-capacity project usable by learners as ungraded practice. Week 8 gains an optional project guide with the project's model, parameters and tasks, a worked example on a separate normalized model, a rehearsal model and four open rehearsal practice items; five project milestones are Case studio self-checks with a week-9 project record. The kLa lab's dataset link now points to the package-pinned CSV instead of a mutable repository URL, and the numeric-answer limitation, which still counted 67 answers, is recounted. The inactive project draft is unchanged; the course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

limitations: All four former compact legacy units now have expanded primers beside the other readings, including one synthetic-data virtual lab; this package is not equivalent to a full university semester.

A proposed 14-week schedule exists but is unmeasured and unreviewed. There is one synthetic-data virtual lab and no substantive homework sequence, laboratory sequence, midterm or cumulative final. An optional oxygen-capacity project guide with rehearsal practice and Case studio milestone self-checks (weeks 8–9) is ungraded practice; the separate project draft stays inactive.

Practice items are short formative checks (two to three per expanded prototype unit and six to nine per original lesson); they do not demonstrate comprehensive outcome coverage or mastery, and objective associations remain provisional.
Bloom labels and structured prerequisite edges are initial authoring classifications awaiting subject-matter review.
Question answers and solution feedback are intentionally public practice authoring specifications, not restricted exam keys.
Of the 89 numerical answers in this package, 12 require a unit, 8 check significant figures and none checks dimensions; the others accept a number within a stated tolerance, with the unit optional.
Total workload and weekly duration are unknown; former nominal credit values and hardcoded reading times do not establish workload.

All cultures, vessels, cell lines and numbers are synthetic teaching examples; this package gives no laboratory protocols, process recipes or medical advice and says nothing about any real cell line, vessel or process. The formulas are first-order textbook estimates, not design methods. The log-reduction example is only simplified arithmetic, not a validated sterilization condition or sterility claim.
The added elemental balance is a synthetic, fixed-coefficient example with a stipulated biomass formula and symbolic product; it does not predict a real cell composition, pathway, or yield.

The oxygen-capacity project is optional and ungraded. Its five milestones are Case studio self-checks whose private drafts are never submitted or scored; the rehearsal practice uses a separate normalized model, and no software check evaluates a learner's derivation or written interpretation. Milestone weeks are planning suggestions, not measured workload or deadlines.
intentionally_omitted: Graded assessments, an activated integrative project and a laboratory sequence are not authored yet (one synthetic-data virtual lab exists); the original lessons extend a partial package.
